transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I’ve been hearing voices… mostly in my apartment. Sometimes in quiet museum rooms too, when no one’s there. It sounds like women whispering behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, like shadows, figures, or anything unusual?

I don’t really see figures, no. It’s more… I hear them. Clear voices, mostly at home, sometimes in empty rooms at the museum. Women whispering behind the walls, saying which photographs belong in the archive.
Do the voices ever talk about you directly, or make you feel like they are controlling what you do?

They don’t exactly say “you” all the time… it’s more like they’re whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs should go in the archive. It feels directed at what I’m doing, I guess.
Do you believe that the photographs you’re archiving have special significance or that you have a special role in deciding which ones belong?

Yes… I do. I think the Caribbean photographs matter more than they understand. The board, and some people with the city arts office… I’m pretty sure they’ve been watching my phone because they know the archive could change how the galleries tell the truth. No one’s really shown me anything that proves I’m wrong.
Do you believe that your work with the photographs has a special purpose or meaning that others don't understand, beyond preserving the truth about the Caribbean?

Yes. I think it’s more than just preserving things. They know the archive would change how the galleries tell the truth… that’s why the board and the city arts people have been watching my phone. I don’t really see another explanation.
Do you feel that the things happening around you, like the voices or being watched, are connected to a larger mission or purpose that only you can fulfill?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like calling it a mission, but the archive is important. They know it could change how the galleries tell the truth, and that’s why I’m sure the board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. No one’s shown me anything that proves otherwise.
Have there been times when you heard the voices or believed you were being watched, even when you weren’t feeling particularly down or excited emotionally?

Yes… there was a stretch, a few weeks maybe, where I wasn’t especially up or anything. Not feeling grand. But I still heard whispers in the apartment, and I still thought the arts people were monitoring my phone.
Have you ever had any beliefs or thoughts that others have told you aren’t true, that aren’t related to the archive, the photographs, or being watched?
I don’t know… not really. I can’t think of anything separate from all that. Maybe people would say I’m wrong about other things, but nothing comes to mind.
Have you had times when you experienced the voices or other strange things happening that lasted for weeks or more, even when your mood was stable and you weren’t feeling unusually down or excited?

Yes… I think I already mentioned that. There were a few weeks where my mood was pretty steady. I wasn’t especially energized or feeling grand. But I still heard the whispers in my apartment, and I still felt sure the arts people were monitoring my phone.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or suspicions that people around you didn’t share, even if they weren’t related to the photographs or being watched?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, people don’t always agree with me, but nothing unusual like that comes to mind.
Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that you know are definitely true, even when others tell you there’s no evidence for them?

I suppose… yes. I’m sure the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth. People say there’s no evidence, but no one has shown me anything that proves I’m wrong.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least a month where you experienced things like hearing voices or believing something strongly that others didn’t, without feeling especially depressed or overly excited?

Yes. For a few weeks, I wasn’t really up or grand or anything like that… my mood was fairly even. But I still heard the whispers in my apartment, and I still believed the arts people were watching my phone.
Do you ever believe in things that you know most people would find strange or impossible, like being able to read minds, being sent messages through the TV, or having special powers?

Not like reading minds or powers. But… yes, I do believe the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive matters, that it would change how the galleries tell the truth. People act like that’s strange, but no one’s shown me anything that proves I’m wrong.
Have you ever held onto a belief that others told you wasn’t true, even when there was no connection to the archive, the photographs, or being watched?
I don’t think so. Not that I can recall, anyway. Most of what people argue with me about is tied to those things.

Have you ever believed in something that you know most people would consider impossible or extremely strange, like being able to hear thoughts through the walls or receiving secret messages that no one else can detect?

Not hearing thoughts through walls, no. But… I do believe they’ve been monitoring my phone. The museum board, the city arts people. They know what my Caribbean archive would mean for the galleries, and nobody’s really proven to me that it isn’t happening.
Have you ever had strong beliefs that others don’t share, even when you weren’t hearing any voices or feeling unusually down or excited, and those beliefs lasted for a month or more?

Yes. It’s not really about moods or voices. I’ve believed for a long time that the museum board and the city arts people have been watching my phone because of my Caribbean archive. They know it could change how the galleries tell the truth. No one has shown me otherwise.
